class.name: AnchoredPoseModifier3D
class.brief_description: Holds a stored pose (a hand around an item, for example) relative to a node, so it follows that node.
class.description: This [SkeletonModifier3D] stores a pose of some bones and puts the skeleton in it. Bones that have no parent bone (the target bones of an IK chain such as [TwoBoneIK3D]) are stored relative to [member anchor_node], so they follow it wherever it goes: a hand stays on a flashlight that trails behind the camera. All other bones (fingers, for example) store their local pose. It is also the editing tool for such a pose. Turn on [member editing] in the editor and the held pose is written into the skeleton's stored bone poses, so the normal tools (the Skeleton3D pose mode, the inspector, undo) work on it. What you change is stored in the modifier. [member preview_anchor] shows the anchor even when the scene hides it (the game shows it later), so the hand can be posed against it. Put this node under the [Skeleton3D], above the IK modifiers that use the target bones. In the game, set [member holding] to make the pose fade in and out. [b]Note:[/b] A modifier never changes the stored bone poses, only what is drawn. That is why the bones of a modified skeleton look unposed in the inspector, and why [member editing] exists.

method.name: capture_bone
method.description: Stores the current pose of [param bone] into the held pose. A bone without a parent is stored relative to the anchor.

method.name: clear_pose
method.description: Removes every bone from the held pose.

method.name: engage
method.description: Uses [param pose] relative to [param anchor] instead of this node's own pose, fading in over [param fade_in] seconds (negative: [member fade_time]). It lasts until [method release]. A [PoseTarget3D] does this for you.

method.name: engage_pose_skeleton
method.description: Like [method engage], but the pose is what the bones of [param pose_skeleton] are at every moment, so animating them animates the pose. Bones without a parent follow [param anchor] (they are in the skeleton's space relative to it), unless they are in [param body_bones]. A [PoseTarget3D] does this with its pose skeleton.

method.name: erase_pose_bone
method.description: Removes [param bone] from the held pose.

method.name: get_blend
method.description: Returns how far the pose has faded in, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].

method.name: get_pose_bone
method.description: Returns the stored transform of [param bone]: relative to the anchor for a bone without a parent, the local pose for any other bone.

method.name: get_pose_bones
method.description: Returns the names of the bones in the held pose.

method.name: has_pose_bone
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param bone] is in the held pose.

method.name: import_pose_from_animation
method.description: Stores the pose that the position, rotation and scale tracks of [param animation] have at [param time]. The track paths only need to end in the bone name ([code]Skeleton3D:Bone[/code]). A bone without a parent is stored relative to the anchor as it is now, so its keys are taken as being in the skeleton's space.

method.name: release
method.description: Ends [method engage]. The pose fades out over the [code]fade_out[/code] it was engaged with, then this node's own pose is used again.

method.name: write_pose_resource
method.description: Copies this node's pose into [member pose_resource] (a new one is made if it is empty), to save as a file and use on [PoseTarget3D] nodes.

method.name: set_pose_bone
method.description: Stores [param transform] as the pose of [param bone]. For a bone without a parent it is in the skeleton's space (it is stored relative to the anchor as it is now). For any other bone it is the local pose.

members.member: The node the bones without a parent follow (the held item). Its scale is ignored.
Bones without a parent that are stored in the skeleton's space (they follow the body) instead of relative to the anchor.
Editor only. Shows the pose even when [member holding] is [code]false[/code]. A preview of another character turns it off.

Editor only, not saved. While [code]true[/code], the held pose is written into the skeleton's stored bone poses and every change made to them is taken into the held pose. The original stored poses are put back when this is turned off and while the scene is saved.
Seconds the pose takes to fade in and out when [member holding] changes (in the game).
Whether the pose is held. The editor always shows it.
The held pose: bone name to [Transform3D]. Use the methods to change it.
Where the pose is moved to and from with the "Write the pose into the resource" and "Read the pose from the resource" buttons.

The bones this modifier poses, as the roots of their subtrees: for example the arm's IK target bone and the elbow's, which take the whole hand with them. A [PoseTarget3D] makes its pose skeleton from these bones.
Editor only. Shows [member anchor_node] while editing even if the scene hides it. It is hidden again before the scene is saved.
A name for this modifier, which a [PoseTarget3D] with the same [member PoseTarget3D.slot] poses. For example [code]right_hand[/code].
If [code]true[/code], when the target is further than the limb can reach, the root bone leans towards it so the hand still gets there.
The leaning starts when the target is further than this fraction of the limb's length.

How much the root bone keeps the distance between the shoulder and the target at what it is at rest, by moving away when the target comes closer (and towards it when it goes further). [code]1.0[/code] keeps the elbow bend the same when the anchor sways to the sides. The rest distance is measured in the editor and saved with the scene. Use the shoulder bone itself as [member reach_root_bone] to leave the other arm alone.
The distance from the shoulder to the target at rest. Set by the editor while the node is shown.

The middle joint of the limb (the elbow). The limb's length is the distance from [member reach_start_bone] to this bone plus the distance from it to [member reach_tip_bone], in the rest pose. If empty, the length is measured by walking up the parents of the tip bone to the start bone, which fails when the tip hangs on an IK target bone.
The bone that leans (for arms: the bone both shoulders hang on).
The first bone of the limb (the shoulder).
The posed bone without a parent that has to be reached (the hand's IK target).
The last bone of the limb (the wrist).
